evidence_summary: Tone Machines identifies Applied Audio as the builder of Guild's VW-1 Volume Wah in the same OEM relationship period as the FW-3; the model is kept separate from the FW-3 because it is a distinct marketed design.

Tone Machines documents the 1974 Guild SP-5 as an Applied-built U.S. reintroduction of the Shin-Ei Surf Wah family. It is a later Applied production state and should not be merged with the earlier Japanese Guild HA-9P/Cromwell-era lineage.

Tone Machines identifies the rare Guild Dimensional Reverb System among Applied Audio's Guild-era OEM products. Retained research-only until model-specific surviving documentation can be cross-checked.

Nomad Banshee Fuzz is documented as an Applied-built New Jersey effect distributed by LIMMCO. The manufacturing date remains unresolved, so 1968 is retained as a documented debut/public window rather than a firm factory start date.

Applied-branded Banshee is documented alongside the Nomad version. The Banshee appears closely related to the fuzz section of the Applied FT-100, but the chronology between Banshee and FT-100 remains unresolved.

physical_builder: LIMMCO initial production; later contractor states unresolved/UMI candidate
evidence_summary: Tone Machines documents LIMMCO initially producing Kimberly's Buzz Box and Volume Expander in its own Long Island warehouse, then hiring outside production. A later redesign is attributed by specialist reconstruction to UMI, while Applied Audio is considered the likely intermediate contractor, but this should not be collapsed into a single-builder record.

The rare Nomad Super Fuzz appears to be a germanium Fuzzrite-type OEM unit, but its relationship to the later LIMMCO/Nomad/Applied family is not established. The specialist source explicitly treats this as a separate unresolved mystery.

model_or_family: HA-9P Surf Wah / early Surf Wah state
evidence_summary: The earlier Guild HA-9P Surf Wah belongs to the Shin-Ei-derived Surf Wah family and predates the 1974 Applied-built SP-5. It is explicitly retained as a separate production state so the Guild branding does not imply continuous Applied manufacture.
